items.stem: A hormone raises blood calcium when levels fall, and its secretion stops once calcium returns to normal. Which type of control does this describe?

options.rationale: Correct: the response opposes and corrects the original change, then switches off.
Positive feedback amplifies a change, as in blood clotting or labour, rather than correcting it.
Feedforward acts before a change occurs; here the gland responds to a change already detected.
Open-loop control has no sensing of the output; here calcium is sensed and the response adjusts.

items.explanation: Correct: the response opposes and corrects the original change, then switches off.

items.stem: Blood returning to the heart from the body tissues first enters which chamber?

options.rationale: Correct: deoxygenated systemic blood returns via the venae cavae into the right atrium.
The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs, not from the body tissues.
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood out to the body; it does not receive venous return.
Blood reaches the right ventricle only after passing through the right atrium.

items.explanation: Correct: deoxygenated systemic blood returns via the venae cavae into the right atrium.

items.stem: Which TWO structures are part of the nephron, the functional unit of the kidney? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: the glomerulus is the filtering capillary tuft of the nephron.
Correct: the proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs much of the filtrate and is part of the nephron.
The alveolus is the gas-exchange sac of the lung, not part of the nephron.
The sarcomere is the contractile unit of muscle, unrelated to the kidney.

items.explanation: Correct: the glomerulus is the filtering capillary tuft of the nephron.
